title: The awaiter pattern
sub: Why you can await almost anything
cards/0/title: await works with anything that has GetAwaiter
cards/0/body:
await x compiles to roughly this: get x.GetAwaiter(); if IsCompleted, call GetResult() right away; if not, subscribe with OnCompleted and return.

It's a pattern, not an interface: any type with the right methods works, even through an extension method.
cards/1/pairs/2/1: What to call when it's done
cards/1/pairs/3/1: Take the result or the exception
cards/2/title: Your own awaitable in two lines
cards/2/body: Add a GetAwaiter extension method for TimeSpan, and you can await a span of time directly.
cards/3/options/0: TimeSpan got a GetAwaiter extension method, and that's all await needs
cards/3/explain: The compiler looks for GetAwaiter the same way foreach looks for GetEnumerator.
cards/4/explain: First the awaiter, then the readiness check.
cards/5/q: What does GetResult() do if the task failed?
cards/5/options/2: Returns an AggregateException as a value
cards/5/explain: That's why await throws the original exception.
cards/6/q: What can you await? Select all that apply.
cards/6/options/4: An int with no GetAwaiter of its own
cards/6/explain: All of them except int have a GetAwaiter.
cards/7/options/0: To force the method to give up control and resume a bit later through the queue
cards/7/options/1: To wait one frame in Unity
cards/7/explain: YieldAwaitable always reports IsCompleted = false, so the method is guaranteed to pause.
